history.summary: Identity confirmed: one of the four Siddh Peeths (Chaar Siddh Peeth) of Dehradun - Laxman Siddh, Kalu Siddh, Manak Siddh and Mandu Siddh - traditionally linked to the disciples of Sage Dattatreya (the 84 Siddhas). Two legends are told: that Rama's brother Laxman did penance here to expiate the killing of Ravana (hence 'Laxman Sidhapith'), and that the saint Swami Laxman Siddh meditated here, took samadhi, and was cremated at this spot; an Akhand Dhuna (eternal sacred fire) is maintained. A pond ~400 m away is said to have been filled by Laxman striking the earth with his arrow. The temple stands deep in Lachhiwala sal forest on the Dehradun-Haridwar/Rishikesh highway near Harrawala (~12 km from Dehradun). Visiting all four Siddh Peeths in one day while fasting is believed to fulfil wishes. FLAG: coordinates are approximate, sourced from a map place listing (verify).

name: Laxman Siddh Temple
town: Harrawala, Dehradun (CSV town 'Dehradun' is the city; the temple is ~12 km southeast near Harrawala on the Haridwar-Rishikesh Road)
town_description: Dehradun is the capital city of Uttarakhand, set in the Doon Valley at the foothills of the Himalayas. Known as the 'School Capital of India' with institutions like The Doon School and the Forest Research Institute, it is also the gateway to the hill station of Mussoorie and a base for Char Dham pilgrims. Harrawala is a locality southeast of the city on the Dehradun-Haridwar/Rishikesh highway, on the edge of the Lachhiwala sal forest.

travel.airport: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun (approx. 15-20 km, on the same Haridwar-Rishikesh highway)
travel.railway: Dehradun Railway Station (approx. 12 km); Harrawala halt is about 1.2 km away
travel.road: On the Dehradun-Haridwar/Rishikesh highway near Harrawala, about 12 km from Dehradun; bus or taxi to Harrawala, then a short walk/trek (~1 km) into the forest

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Sundays draw large crowds; the Laxman Siddh Fair is held on the last Sunday of April
